title: Stowaway Sessions — UX & proto notes
content:
High-level idea (one-liner):
A lightweight, user-visible session snapshot that can be stowed to background storage and resumed later with partial warmup so conversational experiences feel instant while keeping GPU costs bounded.

Motivation / problem: (notes to self)
- Users expect near-instant assistant responses across sessions. Warm starts are expensive (KV warmup, model context priming).
- Full session persistence (hot memory on GPU) is costly at scale; Dedicated customers can afford more, hosted tier needs cheaper tail strategies.
- We have lots of half-used sessions: short gaps (minutes->hours) where a quick resume would improve UX massively.

What Stowaway Sessions should do (concept):
- Capture a small serialized representation of session state periodically (compact KV subset, summary tokens, high-confidence few-shot prompts).
- Store stowed snippet in a cheap, low-latency store (S3/redis tier) with metadata for versioning and model compatibility.
- On resume: attempt a fast-path restore that rehydrates essential state (prefix + cached KV fragments) and issues a background warmup that continues loading larger KV as the user interacts.
- Provide UX affordance: indicator that "Assistant is resuming, responses may be partial for 1–3 turns" with graceful fallback.

User stories (raw):
- As a returning user, I want my previous chat context to be available immediately so I don't need to remind the assistant what we were doing.
- As a product manager, I want restart latency <200ms for the first reply for short-gap sessions while ensuring long-term storage costs remain low.
- As an SRE, I want stowed snapshots to be safe against model upgrades and to have eviction policies to bound storage usage.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics (first-pass):
- 80% of resumes after 2–30 minutes return a first reply <250ms (server time) and maintain coherence with last 3 user turns in >90% of sampled evals.
- Average storage per stowed session <4KB compressed.
- Cost model: incremental storage + restore CPU/GPU cost adds <5% to per-session cost versus cold-start baseline for hosted tier.
- Noise / privacy: snapshots include no raw user-provided PII; redact except for conversation markers / assistant instructions.

Sketch of data model / fields to persist (brain dump):
- session_id, last_active_ts, model_name+version, stow_version (proto), compressed_prefix (1–3 recent turns tokens), compacted_kv_signatures (hashes + small hot keys), user-scoped metadata (language, persona tag), confidence_scores, policy_flags (do_not_persist), hmac/signature for integrity.

Restore flow (prefetch & gradual warmup):
1) Client reconnect -> call /sessions/resume(session_id).
2) Check model compatibility and fetch stowed snippet from store (fast path in redis if <TTL, else S3).
3) Return immediate synthesized reply from compacted_prefix (assistant acts on that snapshot) while enqueuing background warmup job to rehydrate full KV on a warm GPU or local caching layer.
4) If user asks a follow-up requiring long memory, hold or fetch full state; show small loading UI if needed.

Edge cases / questions / open items: 
- How to handle model variant mismatch (quantized vs full) — fallback to textual prefix-only resume and mark degraded quality.
- Security: snapshots may contain sensitive tokens from context; must run redaction pipeline (what heuristics?).
- TTL / eviction: default 7 days? cheaper tier 24h? enterprise-configurable.
- Multi-device concurrency: last-writer-wins vs merge heuristics.
- Cost tradeoff: maintain redis hot cache for warm resumes vs cold fetch from object store.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Target: hosted API only, one mid-sized LM (redwood/open-medium-1), opt-in flag for 10% of sessions.
- Implement minimal serializer that keeps last 2 turns + 3 hashed KV keys + metadata. Store in redis with 24h TTL.
- Instrument metrics: resume_latency, resume_success_coherence (micro-eval), storage_bytes_per_session, cost_delta_per_session.
- UX: simple banner "Restored previous chat — still warming up" + autoswitch if degraded.

Rollout / ops notes: 
- Need small k8s workers for background rehydrates that can spill to Dedicated pools.
- Add console dashboard: per-route stow success rate, avg resume latency, storage usage.
- Migration: stow_version field to support deserialization across schema changes.

Implementation TODOs (owner: Maxine) — checklist:
- [ ] proto shape + serializer POC (Python)
- [ ] redaction heuristics + unit tests (collab Mika)
- [ ] redis S3 store abstraction + TTL config (collab Noah)
- [ ] resume API + fast-path response generator (API team)
- [ ] UX banner copy + experiment gating (Jillian)
- [ ] small micro-eval harness and internal dataset for coherence checks

Quick notes to revisit:
- Could we piggyback on existing KV cache signatures (Sana/IQBAL work) to make stow tiny?
- Consider a "cheap snapshot tier" that stores only assistant instructions for low-value sessions.
- How does this interact with session pin/keep-alive features in Dedicated?

Unresolved items to bring to sync with Eng: list of model-internal hooks we can use for quick KV serialization (ask serving-runtime).

Random ideas (parking lot):
- "Ghost warmup": proactively warm most-likely sessions during user inactivity windows based on heuristics.
- Allow user control: pin this chat to stay hot for X hours (paid feature).
- Snapshot diffs for bandwidth-limited clients: client stores deltas to reduce server storage.

Notes end — rough/iterative. Will formalize into a lightweight PRD once POC numbers available.

Slack threads / references:
- #session-econ thread (search: "stowaway")
- related doc: "kv-cache-deep-dive-playpad" (Sana Iqbal)

Last thought: prioritize small, auditable snapshot that avoids PII and model internals; UX wins are disproportionate for small wins in latency.
